_provenance: Second pass on 2026-08-16. The first recorded a reported $2T listing expectation; the same scan then surfaced Business Insider carrying $1.5 trillion. Both are expectations for the same unpriced listing, and neither is a transaction. Recording the spread rather than one number, because the spread is the honest reading: the market does not know, and the width of the disagreement is itself the information.

reported_ipo_expectation_bn.note: Ruling R2: a listing expectation never anchors.

reported_ipo_expectation_bn.source: New York Post and three other outlets, Aug 13 2026

ipo_expectation_spread.value: Reported listing expectations run $1.5T to $2.0T against a $965B last completed mark, so between 1.6 and 2.1 times
ipo_expectation_spread.note: A $500B spread on an unpriced listing is not a forecast, it is a measure of how little is known. The S-1 closes it.
